title: Pizzoccheri (Buckwheat Pasta with Savoy Cabbage, Potato and Fontina)
summary: Buckwheat ribbon pasta cooked with potato and cabbage, layered with fontina and Parmesan, and finished with a nutty garlic-sage butter.
equipment: baking tray dusted with buckwheat flour
ovenproof serving dish about 23 x 33 cm

ingredients.item: buckwheat flour, plus extra for dusting
waxy potatoes, peeled, in 2 cm cubes
savoy cabbage, cored, leaves torn into 4 cm pieces
fine salt for 5 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 6.75 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: fontina (or another Alpine cheese), thinly sliced

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the buckwheat and plain flours in a large bowl, add the water, and stir to combine. Knead for 5 minutes into a soft, slightly tacky dough, similar in feel to modelling clay - buckwheat has no gluten of its own, so it never turns elastic, and it's the plain flour that holds everything together.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover the dough and rest it for 15 minutes before rolling.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll the dough out on a dusted worktop to 2-3 mm thick, then cut it into 7 cm wide strips and across into 1 cm ribbons. Spread the ribbons out on a flour-dusted tray as you go.

steps.title: Warm the oven and dish
steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan) and put the serving dish inside to warm through - a warm dish keeps the cheese melting as you layer, rather than seizing against a cold surface.

steps.title: Cook potatoes, cabbage and pasta
steps.text: Bring 5 litres of water to the boil with the 40 g salt. Add the potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, then add the cabbage and pasta together and cook for a further 6-8 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the pasta is cooked but still firm.

steps.title: Layer with cheese
steps.text: Using a spider strainer, lift a third of the pasta and vegetables straight into the warmed dish and scatter over a third of the fontina and Parmesan. Repeat twice more, finishing with cheese on top - the heat left in the pasta and vegetables is what melts each layer of cheese as you go.

steps.title: Make the garlic-sage butter
steps.text: Melt the butter with the garlic and sage in a small frying pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, until the garlic turns golden and the butter smells nutty rather than just melted.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Pour the hot butter over the layered dish, then toss everything together once at the table so the cheese, butter and pasta combine. Season with the pepper and serve immediately, while it's all still molten.

tips: Don't over-knead expecting elasticity - buckwheat dough stays soft and slightly tacky rather than springy, and that's normal.

If the dough cracks at the edges or crumbles as you roll, it's too dry: work in 1 tablespoon of warm water and knead for a minute. Small tears are fine, just press them together, since the ribbons are cut short anyway.
Warm the serving dish before layering; a cold dish will cause the cheese to seize instead of melting into the pasta.
Cook the potatoes a few minutes ahead of the cabbage and pasta so everything finishes tender at the same time rather than the potato being underdone.
Watch the garlic closely in the butter - it should turn golden, not brown, or it will taste bitter.
storage: Best eaten straight away while the cheese is molten, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan or microwave until piping hot throughout, adding a splash of water if it looks dry. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
